1. Read what the Big Muff Pi is.

## What it is

- The **Big Muff Pi** came out in **1969**, made by **Electro-Harmonix** of New York (Wikipedia, "Big Muff").
- Three knobs: **Volume**, **Tone** and **Sustain** (the gain). The first version put them in a triangle.
- Four transistor stages: an input booster, two clipping stages, a tone stack, an output booster (Wikipedia).

## How it makes its sound

- Each clipping stage has two diodes in its feedback: they stop the wave growing past about 0.6 V, a *soft* clip. Two in a row: the second clips what the first already clipped, so the sound is very compressed and sustains for a long time.
- The **tone stack** mixes a low-pass and a high-pass. At noon both are partly down around **1 kHz**: a **mid scoop** (Wikipedia: less midrange; ~1 kHz from a student report found by search). Turn Tone left for the low-pass (dark), right for the high-pass (thin).
- The output booster makes up the level the tone stack loses.

## The pedal

The Big Muff Pi's face, drawn after photos (positions approximate, no logos). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), click the footswitch to bypass, then press a ▶ button. The guitar is this site's pickup model (pick one, and its volume, below the buttons); the sound goes through the pedal model, then a clean amp. Nobody has compared it with a real pedal. The picture shows the waveform going in and coming out.

<div class="pdp" data-pedal="bigmuff"></div>

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="bigmuff" data-set="{&quot;sustain&quot;:7,&quot;tone&quot;:5}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Sustain 7, Tone noon.</b> The classic: thick, scooped.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="bigmuff" data-set="{&quot;sustain&quot;:7,&quot;tone&quot;:0}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Tone fully left.</b> The low-pass alone: dark and woolly.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="bigmuff" data-set="{&quot;sustain&quot;:7,&quot;tone&quot;:10}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Tone fully right.</b> The high-pass alone: thin and fizzy.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="bigmuff" data-set="{&quot;sustain&quot;:10,&quot;tone&quot;:6}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Sustain 10.</b> A lead note that lasts and lasts.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="bigmuff" data-set="{&quot;sustain&quot;:2,&quot;tone&quot;:5}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Sustain 2.</b> Still fuzzy: the two clipping stages have their own gain.</p></div>
```

Click an answer. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="pd-q" data-a="1"><p><b>What does the Big Muff&#x27;s tone stack do at noon?</b></p><ul><li>Boosts the mids</li><li>Scoops the mids</li><li>Removes the bass only</li><li>Nothing</li></ul><p class="pd-why">Low-pass + high-pass blended: a dip around 1 kHz.</p></div>
<div class="pd-q" data-a="2"><p><b>Which knob sets the gain?</b></p><ul><li>Volume</li><li>Tone</li><li>Sustain</li></ul><p class="pd-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="pd-q" data-a="1"><p><b>How many clipping stages?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li><li>Four</li></ul><p class="pd-why">Two, each with a diode pair in its feedback.</p></div>
```
